sources.entry: ast-grep-cli - A CLI tool for structural code search, linting, and rewriting based on syntax trees.

summary.one_liner: ast-grep (sg) is a CLI tool that searches, lints, and rewrites code by matching abstract syntax tree patterns written like ordinary code.
summary.what_it_does: ast-grep is a command-line tool for structural code search, linting, and rewriting. Instead of matching plain text like grep, it matches abstract syntax tree nodes using patterns written in the target language's own syntax. The README says `$` followed by uppercase letters (e.g. `$MATCH`) acts as a wildcard that matches any single AST node. Users can run one-off searches and rewrites from the command line with --pattern, --rewrite, and --lang flags. It also supports YAML configuration files for writing lint rules or code modifications. The README describes it as built on tree-sitter parsing, written in a compiled language, and using multiple cores. It also mentions a jQuery-like API for AST traversal and manipulation.
use_cases: search codebase by code structure rather than text
rewrite code patterns across a project
write custom lint rules in YAML
migrate code after library breaking changes
notable: Patterns look like ordinary source code, using $UPPERCASE wildcards to match any AST node
Search and rewrite based on syntax trees rather than text, so formatting differences do not block matches
YAML rule configuration for custom lint checks and code modifications
Installable through many channels including npm, pip, cargo, homebrew, scoop, and nix-shell
Listed in vinta/awesome-python under Code Analysis
caveats: README does not state a license; the license field is unknown from the text provided
README does not list supported languages beyond examples in TypeScript
Building from source requires installing rustup and cloning the repository
